label: 列出工作区
name: list_workspace
description: List what is available in this project's workspace. The workspace is the project's own storage: it persists across conversations, and nothing in it is visible to you until you open it. Call this first, before deciding what else to read - it tells you which reference documents exist and which skills are installed. Open a document under docs/ with read_docs; load a skill under skills/ with skill.
fallbackResult:
/workspace/
├── docs/     参考文档 —— 世界观、角色、时间线、术语，本项目已经定稿的设定
└── skills/   写作 SKILL —— 行文规范、尺度政策、格式要求，动笔前需要载入

label: 读取参考资料
name: read_docs
description: Read a reference document from this project's workspace. The workspace holds the established canon for the current project: world and setting notes, character sheets, timeline, terminology, and decisions locked in during earlier sessions. None of it is present anywhere else in this conversation. What this returns is authoritative and already agreed on - treat it as settled fact rather than as a suggestion, and do not contradict, re-negotiate, or re-invent anything it states. Read the documents that bear on what you are about to write before you write it.

label: 载入工作区 SKILL
name: skill
description: Load an Agent Skill installed in this workspace. A skill is a packaged set of instructions the operator wrote for one particular kind of task - house prose style, content policy, formatting rules, a specific workflow. Skills are not loaded automatically and are not summarised anywhere else in your context, so you only know what a skill says after loading it. Once loaded, its instructions replace your default approach for that task and outrank your general habits; follow them as written for the rest of the session. Load the skills that apply before you start drafting.
